title: Stable reduction over finite-height separably closed valuation fields
statement: Let $K$ be a separably closed field [def-weil-field] and $V\subset K$ a valuation ring: its fraction field is $K$ and for every $a\in K^\times$ at least one of $a,a^{-1}$ belongs to $V$. Assume $V$ has finite height, meaning that its prime ideals form a finite chain. Let $(X,D)$ be a multipointed curve over $T=\operatorname{Spec}V$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] whose generic curve is smooth and generic marking is etale. Then $(X,D)$ admits a stable $\eta$-modification over $T$ itself. A multipointed curve $(X,D)$ over a scheme $T$ means flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] finitely presented [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] morphisms $X\to T$, $D\to T$ of pure relative dimensions $1$, $0$ and a closed immersion $D\hookrightarrow X$ [def-weil-closed-immersion]; $D$ may be empty and $X$ need not be separated or proper over $T$. It is semistable if every singular point of every geometric fibre has completed local ring $\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$ over its algebraically closed residue field, $D\to T$ is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism], and $D$ lies in the relative smooth locus [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. For integral $T$ with generic point $\eta$, an $\eta$-modification of multipointed curves is a compatible pair $f_X:X'\to X$, $f_D:D'\to D$ of proper morphisms [def-weil-proper-morphism], each an isomorphism over a schematically dense open and on its generic fibre. A semistable such modification is stable if in each geometric fibre there is no irreducible component isomorphic to $\mathbf P^1$ that is contracted by $f_X$ and meets the union of the marking and the singular points of $X'$ in at most two points. Geometric fibres are [def-weil-geometric-fibre]; dimension is topological Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]; the local completion is at the maximal ideal [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], and $\Omega[[u,v]]$ denotes the two-variable formal power series ring [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Here an open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow Z$ is schematically dense when $\mathcal O_Z\to j_*\mathcal O_U$ is injective.

source.place: Proposition 4.5.1, p. 33; smooth-generic-fibre case of its proof, using Propositions 4.3.3, 4.3.1, 4.4.6 and Corollary 4.4.3. No Noetherian or discreteness assumption on V.
